RATE REGULATION DIVISION
PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS
OCTOBER 16, 2026


ATTACHMENTS:
Attachment AN-1		Regulatory Resumé of Adrian Narvaez 	


PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS 
Q.	Please state your name and business address.
A.	Adrian Narvaez, Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission), 1701 N. Congress Avenue, Austin, TX 78711-3326.
Q.	By whom are you employed and in what capacity?
A.	I am employed by the Commission as a Rate Analyst in the Tariff and Rate Analysis Section of the Rate Regulation Division.
Q.	What are your responsibilities as a Rate Analyst for the Commission?
A.	My principal responsibility is analyzing utility filings on matters relating to rate design and cost allocation.  My responsibilities include analyzing electric industry regulatory policy, reviewing tariffs to determine compliance with Commission requirements, and preparing and presenting testimony as an expert witness on cost allocation and rate design issues in contested proceedings before the Commission and the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH).
Q.	Please state your educational background and professional experience.
A.	Attachment AN-1 contains a summary of my regulatory experience and educational background.
Q.	Have you previously filed testimony before the Commission?
A.	Yes.  Attachment AN-1 contains a listing of direct testimonies I have filed at the Commission.
PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF TESTIMONY
Q.	What is the purpose of your testimony in this proceeding?
A.	My testimony regarding El Paso Electric Company’s (EPE or the Company) application will address, in whole or in part, the following issues from the Commission’s Preliminary Order issued on July 9, 2026:
8.	Is it appropriate for the ESA not to be subject to review or approval by the Commission?
9.	What, if any, conditions should be placed on approval to ensure that Texas residential and small commercial customers are not unreasonably affected by approval of EPE’s application?

III.	SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS
Q.	What is your recommendation?
A.	I recommend that: 
The Commission require that in all future base rate proceedings, EPE must provide testimony and supporting workpapers demonstrating that costs related to providing service to large load customers, including all generation, transmission and other system upgrades made in order to provide service to EPE’s large load customers, have not been shifted to EPE’s other Texas retail customers.
The Commission require EPE to maintain all executed Energy Service Agreements (ESA) and provide them upon request in EPE’s future base rate proceedings.
All ESAs should be subject to review, modification, or approval by the Commission.
The Commission require that in all future base rate proceedings, EPE must demonstrate that all charges, credits, security requirements, and all other terms imposed under executed ESAs are sufficient, administered consistently with the Commission-approved tariff, and comply with PURA and Commission rules. 

HLFLP TARIFF AND ESA
Q.	What is EPE’s proposal in this docket?
A.	EPE requests Commission approval of a new tariff Schedule No. 27- High Load Factor for Large Power Service (HLFLP) for service to very large customers, such as data centers, with peak demand of at least 75 MW and annual load factors of at least 85 percent. EPE’s proposed HLFLP tariff requires qualifying customers to execute an ESA containing customer-specific load commitments, security requirements, facility charge provisions, and other terms designed to protect EPE and its customers from stranded costs and other financial risks. While EPE included a form ESA in its application for informational purposes, EPE stated that it is not requesting Commission approval of the ESA itself. Although EPE states that other large customers have expressed interest, the only confirmed large load customer is Wurldwide LLC whose future data center is currently under construction.  
Q.	What are the rates that EPE is requesting for the HLFLP tariff?
A.	EPE’s proposed tariff included in its application included the retail rates that were previously approved for Wurldwide LLC in Docket No. 56903 under Schedule No. 33A - Large Economic Development Service. Rates for Schedule No. 33A were derived based on the cost of service study requested in Docket No. 52195, EPE’s most recent base rate proceeding at the time that EPE’s application was filed in this docket, and an estimated load profile developed based on expected load ramp and full load conditions for an expected data center customer.
Q.	Will the rates approved in Docket No. 56903 be updated to reflect the cost-of-service data in EPE’s recently concluded base rate case, Docket No. 57568?
A.	Yes. One of the terms in the Stipulation and Settlement Agreement in Docket No. 56903 states that “[R]ates will be updated for new Commission approved cost of service until the customer is active and included in a full rate case proceeding. EPE agrees to file a request to update Rate Schedules 33A and 33B within 90 days of the final order in Docket No. 57568.” In his direct testimony, EPE witness James Schichtl states:
[I]f the revised rates for Schedule 33A are approved while this case is still pending, EPE will amend this filing to incorporate those approved rates. If a final order is entered in this proceeding before revised rates for Schedule 33A are approved, EPE will make a separate filing to request that Schedule 27 be revised accordingly. When Schedule 27 is updated to reflect the revised rates for Schedule 33A, there will no longer be a need for Schedule 33A, and so, at that time, EPE requests that Schedule 33A be terminated.
	EPE filed an application to update Schedules 33A and 33B after the Commission issued an Order in Docket No. 57568. Although Staff issued its recommendation to adopt EPE’s updated rates for Rate Schedules 33A and 33B in Docket No. 59948, the Commission has not yet issued an order in that docket.
Q.	How does EPE state that HLFLP rates will be established in the future?
A.	Mr. Schichtl states that EPE “expects that a very large customer eligible for service under HLFLP (the Wurldwide data center for example) will have their own rate class for cost allocation and ratemaking purposes. If multiple customers ultimately take service under the HLFLP tariff the Company will determine if a combined rate class or customer-specific classes is appropriate.”
Q.	Do you agree with Mr. Schichtl’s proposal regarding the methodology to establish future HLFLP rates?
A.	In general, yes.  I would additionally note that any future determinations by EPE regarding combined or customer-specific rate classes for large load customers are subject to review and approval by the Commission.
Q.	Is it important to ensure that EPE’s non-large load customers do not bear costs associated with providing service to large load customers?
A.	Yes. The expected increase in data centers and other large load customers presents risks that differ significantly from those associated with traditional customer growth. Serving large-load customers requires substantial investments in generation, transmission, and other system infrastructure long before the utility can realize the revenues associated with those loads. While such investments may be justified when the projected load materializes as expected, there is a risk that a project may be delayed, downsized, or ultimately canceled, leaving the Company with facilities that were constructed to serve a customer that does not ultimately take service at the anticipated level. Without appropriate safeguards, the costs associated with these investments could be shifted to EPE’s other customers.
Q.	Aside from the provisions included in EPE’s proposed HLFLP tariff and ESA, do you recommend approval of additional requirements on EPE to ensure that the costs associated with large load customers are not borne by EPE’s other customers? 
A.	Yes. I recommend that in all future base rate proceedings, EPE must provide testimony and supporting workpapers demonstrating that costs related to providing service to large load customers, including all generation, transmission and other system upgrades made in order to provide service to EPE’s large load customers, have not been shifted to EPE’s other Texas retail customers. This requirement will promote transparency and accountability in EPE’s future rate cases and provide the Commission with the information necessary to verify that EPE’s other Texas retail customers are not adversely affected by the Company’s efforts to serve large load customers.
Q.	EPE stated that it did not seek approval of its ESA. Should the Commission have oversight over EPE’s large load customer ESAs?
A.	Yes. While my recommendation that EPE provide workpapers and testimony demonstrating that costs related to providing service to large load customers have not been shifted to EPE’s other Texas retail customers addresses the risk of possible cross-class subsidization, this does not address the fact that the HLFLP tariff grants the Company discretion over several customer-specific terms that are addressed in the ESA. As Mr. Schichtl states in his testimony, “[T]he ESA is used in concert with the HLFLP to establish customer-specific load and security requirements for service and customer protection.” Mr. Schichtl states that “EPE expects that most customers taking service under the new tariff will have a dedicated transmission substation, and the "Facility Charge" designed to recover the associated capital and O&M costs will be incorporated in the ESA.”
			If two similarly situated large load customers receive materially different customer-specific contract terms, or if an ESA’s terms are insufficient to protect the broader body of ratepayers, questions of undue preference or discrimination could arise. Public Utility Regulatory Act § 36.0039(c) states that an electric utility may not “grant an unreasonable preference or advantage concerning rates to a person in a classification” and “subject a person in a classification to an unreasonable prejudice or disadvantage concerning rates.” Furthermore, The ESA appears to allow customer-specific negotiation of security amounts. This could lead to concerns on whether security amounts are fair or sufficient.  
Q.	How should concerns regarding the fairness and sufficiency of ESA customer-specific terms be addressed in the future? 
A.	I recommend that the Commission require EPE to maintain all executed ESAs and provide them upon request in EPE’s future base rate proceedings. Furthermore, I recommend that the Commission require that in all future base rate proceedings, EPE must demonstrate that all charges, credits, security requirements, and all other terms imposed under executed ESAs are sufficient, administered consistently with the Commission-approved tariff, and comply with PURA and Commission rules. This requirement will promote transparency and accountability in EPE’s future rate cases and provide the Commission with the opportunity to verify that the terms included in large load customer ESAs are sufficient and reasonable. 
CONCLUSION
Q.	Please summarize your recommendation?
A.	I recommend that EPE be required to bear the burden in future rate proceedings to protect the broader body of ratepayers from costs incurred to serve large load customers. I recommend that in all future rate proceedings, EPE be required to provide testimony and supporting workpapers demonstrating that costs related to providing service to large load customers, including, but not limited to, all generation, transmission and other system upgrades made in order to provide service to EPE’s large load customers, have not been shifted to EPE’s other Texas retail customers. I also recommend that EPE be required to maintain all executed ESAs and provide them upon request in EPE’s future base rate proceedings. Finally. I recommend that in all future base rate proceedings, EPE must demonstrate that all charges, credits, security requirements, and all other terms imposed under executed ESAs are sufficient, administered consistently with the Commission-approved tariff, and comply with PURA and Commission rules.
Q.      	If you do not address an issue or position in your testimony, should that be interpreted as Staff supporting EPE’s position on that issue? 
A.        No.  The fact that I do not address an issue in my testimony should not be construed as agreeing, endorsing, or consenting to any position taken by EPE.
Q. 	Does this conclude your direct testimony?
A. 	Yes.
